questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. Roads with black ice may look wet. Be careful when temperatures drop below freezing and roads look wet.

questions.question: Containers of hazardous materials must be:

options.text: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
A maximum of four feet tall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Hazardous material containers must be braced so they do not fall, slide, or bounce during transport.

questions.question: A hazardous material's identification number should appear:

options.text: On a sticker near the material's shipping container.

questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the packaging and on the shipping papers. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other large containers.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, your best hope to stop is to:
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, look for a way to stop outside your vehicle. An escape ramp is the safest option.

questions.question: A vehicle should be equipped with all of the following, except:

options.text: Warning devices for parked vehicles, such as flares.

questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry emergency equipment. This includes at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles like warning triangles or flares.

questions.question: Baffled liquid tanks are:

options.text: Tanks that control the surge of liquids with perforated bulkheads.
Tanks that have no bulkheads and allow liquids to move freely.
Tanks that have nothing inside to slow down the flow of liquids.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tanks that control the surge of liquids with perforated bulkheads.
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have bulkheads with holes that let liquid move slowly. This reduces forward and backward surge. These tanks do not prevent side-to-side movement and may still cause rollovers.

questions.question: The minimum acceptable tread depth for rear tires is:
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove. Rear tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: When traveling more slowly than 40 mph, maintain at least ____ of following distance per every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle length. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks are used in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks in their brake systems.

questions.question: When driving, you should stop and take a break ____ to avoid becoming too tired.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, stop for a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles.

questions.question: Your brakes fail while driving downhill and there is no escape ramp. What should you do?
questions.explanation: First look for an escape ramp to stop your vehicle. If no ramp is available, find another safe place to stop. This could be an open field or a side road that is flat or goes uphill.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as possible to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless necessary.

questions.question: If cargo catches fire in a box trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Put a large, heavy blanket over the trailer.

questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire, especially if hazardous materials are inside. Opening the doors adds oxygen to the fire, which makes it grow larger.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle, manhole covers should:
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle before driving. Never drive a tank vehicle if any valves or manhole covers are open.

questions.question: Which action helps avoid distracted driving?

options.text: Only physical distractions cause distracted driving, not mental ones.
Pre-programming radio stations while driving reduces distraction.
Avoid having complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid having complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: Do not have complicated or emotionally intense conversations while driving. Pre-program your radio before you leave. Avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while driving. Remember that mental distractions can be just as dangerous as physical ones.

questions.question: When inspecting a tank vehicle, what is most important to check?

options.text: There is no frost on the windshield.

questions.explanation: Before driving a tank vehicle, check the operator's manual for what to inspect. The most important check is to make sure there are no leaks.

questions.question: When going down a hill, how can you reduce the need for braking?
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, slow down and shift into a lower gear. This helps you control your vehicle without overusing the brakes. Heavy braking downhill can overheat the brakes and reduce their power.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes ahead of you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop at a safe distance and tell police about the aggressive driving.
Block them in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance and tell police about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: Stop safely away from the crash scene. Wait for police to arrive and tell them about the aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings should not be loose, wet with oil or grease, or too thin.

questions.question: When you brake, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it down slowly and smoothly.
Pump it repeatedly, but do not hold it down.
Use the same amount of force every time you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually every time you slow or stop. The amount of brake pressure you need depends on your speed and how quickly you need to stop.
